defect.locator_note: group_inventory line 4 / content_page line 27; disclosed lake records exist only for Karo, Kyllo, and Carpenter.
defect.problem: The rule asserts current DOJ/DHS policy and a leading state decision, but the disclosed evidence contains no DOJ/DHS policy text and no State v. Andrews authority/treatment record. Under the B lens, currency and treatment of those authorities cannot be verified from the disclosed record.
defect.proposed_fix: Add disclosed authority records or policy texts for the DOJ 2015 guidance, DHS 2015 directive, and State v. Andrews, including current treatment/status, or narrow the rule to the three disclosed SCOTUS analogies only.

reasons: The three disclosed SCOTUS analogies are live good law in the lake records, but they do not verify the current force of the DOJ/DHS policy assertions or State v. Andrews.
The statement that there is no controlling Supreme Court cell-site-simulator decision is an absence claim that is not independently verifiable from the limited disclosed corpus.
Defaulting to refuted on uncertainty is required because material parts of the black-letter rule rest on undisclosed authorities.
residual_risks: This is a currency/treatment defect only; support and quote fidelity are outside lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Separate the disclosed SCOTUS analogy from undisclosed policy/state-law assertions, and attach current authority records for each non-SCOTUS source.
